section: Persons in news - appointments, resignations and obituaries
subsections: Heads of state/government elected abroad - country
Heads of international organisations - organisation + term
Women FIRSTs in appointments - post + organisation

accepted.s: Andy Burnham was reported to have become Prime Minister of which country in July 2026 after ousting Keir Starmer as Labour leader?
accepted.x: Andy Burnham became Prime Minister of the United Kingdom in July 2026 after replacing Keir Starmer as Labour leader.
accepted.tq: Use the country association rather than being distracted by leaders from other countries.
accepted.sec: Heads of state/government elected abroad - country

accepted.s: Balendra (Balen) Shah was sworn in as Prime Minister of which country in March 2026?
accepted.x: Balendra Shah was sworn in as Prime Minister of Nepal in March 2026.
accepted.tq: Direct leader–country identification tests a current-affairs appointment.
accepted.sec: Heads of state/government elected abroad - country

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Balendra Shah:
1. He was sworn in as Prime Minister of Nepal in March 2026.
2. He assumed office at the age of 35.
3. His Rastriya Swatantra Party won a majority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: Shah became Nepal’s Prime Minister in March 2026 at 35, and his Rastriya Swatantra Party won a majority.
accepted.tq: Check each statement separately before accepting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Heads of state/government elected abroad - country

accepted.s: Tarique Rahman became Prime Minister of Bangladesh following which political development?
o: A landslide victory of the BNP in the February 2026 election
A constitutional appointment after the resignation of the President
A coalition victory in the 2025 election
accepted.x: Tarique Rahman became Bangladesh’s Prime Minister after the BNP secured a landslide victory in the February 2026 election.
accepted.tq: Link the office-holder with the specific electoral event and date.
accepted.sec: Heads of state/government elected abroad - country

accepted.s: Min Aung Hlaing assumed the civilian office of President of Myanmar in:
accepted.x: Min Aung Hlaing moved into the civilian presidency of Myanmar in April 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish close dates by associating the month with the political transition.
accepted.sec: Heads of state/government elected abroad - country

accepted.s: Delcy Rodríguez became interim President of Venezuela in January 2026 after:
o: the resignation of Nicolás Maduro following an election defeat
the removal of Keir Starmer as Labour leader
accepted.x: Delcy Rodríguez became interim President of Venezuela in January 2026 after the United States seized Nicolás Maduro.
accepted.tq: Identify the event that directly explains the interim succession.
accepted.sec: Heads of state/government elected abroad - country

accepted.s: Giorgia Meloni is notable for which of the following?
o: She became Italy’s first woman Prime Minister and its longest continuously serving post-war Prime Minister.
She became Nepal’s youngest Prime Minister.
She was Japan’s first woman Prime Minister.
She became Venezuela’s first interim President.
accepted.x: Giorgia Meloni is Italy’s first woman Prime Minister and became the longest continuously serving Prime Minister in Italy’s post-war history.
accepted.tq: Combine the office, country and superlative without confusing separate firsts.
accepted.sec: Heads of state/government elected abroad - country

accepted.s: Kirsty Coventry belongs to which country?
accepted.x: Kirsty Coventry, the IOC President, is from Zimbabwe.
accepted.tq: Test the nationality attached to an international office-holder.
accepted.sec: Heads of international organisations - organisation + term

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus is the Director-General of the WHO. Ajay Banga heads the World Bank, Kristalina Georgieva heads the IMF and Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala heads the WTO.
accepted.tq: Use organisation–office-holder pairs and reject swapped international institutions.
accepted.sec: Heads of international organisations - organisation + term

accepted.s: Khalilur Rahman defeated which country’s candidate in the election for President of the 81st UN General Assembly session?
accepted.x: Khalilur Rahman defeated the candidate from Cyprus in the election for the 81st UN General Assembly session.
accepted.tq: Test the less prominent opposing candidate in an international election.
accepted.sec: Heads of international organisations - organisation + term

accepted.s: António Guterres is scheduled to leave office as UN Secretary-General at the end of:
accepted.x: António Guterres is scheduled to leave the office of UN Secretary-General at the end of 2026.
accepted.tq: Read the term-ending year precisely rather than confusing it with the successor’s starting year.
accepted.sec: Heads of international organisations - organisation + term

accepted.s: The five-year term of the successor to António Guterres as UN Secretary-General is scheduled to begin on:
accepted.x: The successor’s five-year term is scheduled to begin on 1 January 2027.
accepted.tq: Separate the selection year from the commencement date of the term.
accepted.sec: Heads of international organisations - organisation + term

accepted.s: In the UNSC straw poll for a candidate for UN Secretary-General, which condition is required?
o: At least 9 ‘Encourage’ votes and no ‘Discourage’ vote from a permanent member
A unanimous vote of all 15 Security Council members
At least 10 ‘Encourage’ votes irrespective of permanent-member votes
A two-thirds vote of the UN General Assembly before the straw poll
accepted.x: A candidate needs at least 9 ‘Encourage’ votes out of 15 and must receive no ‘Discourage’ vote from any permanent member.
accepted.tq: Break a procedural rule into its numerical threshold and veto-related condition.
accepted.sec: Heads of international organisations - organisation + term

accepted.s: Varsha Ashok Aglawe became which numbered Director-General of the Geological Survey of India?
accepted.x: Varsha Ashok Aglawe became the 54th Director-General of the Geological Survey of India, an organisation with a 176-year history.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the office-holder’s serial number from the organisation’s age.
accepted.sec: Women FIRSTs in appointments - post + organisation

accepted.s: Sunetra Pawar became the first woman Deputy Chief Minister of which State?
accepted.x: Sunetra Pawar became the first woman Deputy Chief Minister of Maharashtra after the death of Ajit Pawar.
accepted.tq: Use the State–post association instead of the surrounding succession detail.
accepted.sec: Women FIRSTs in appointments - post + organisation

accepted.s: Dhriti Banerjee became the first woman Director of the:
accepted.x: Dhriti Banerjee became the first woman Director of the Zoological Survey of India. A newly identified skate species was named after her.
accepted.tq: Separate the Zoological Survey from the similarly named Geological Survey.
accepted.sec: Women FIRSTs in appointments - post + organisation

accepted.s: Who was sworn in as the 53rd Chief Justice of India in November 2025?
accepted.x: Justice Surya Kant was sworn in as the 53rd Chief Justice of India in November 2025.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional post with the correct office-holder and serial number.
accepted.sec: Constitutional, statutory and executive appointments

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Mahesh Dixit is the Director of the Intelligence Bureau, not the Cabinet Secretary. T.V. Somanathan is the Cabinet Secretary.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped authority or office-holder in a set of current appointments.
accepted.sec: Constitutional, statutory and executive appointments

accepted.s: T.V. Somanathan received a one-year extension as Cabinet Secretary from the:
accepted.x: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet granted T.V. Somanathan a one-year extension in August 2026.
accepted.tq: Ask which executive authority formally controls the appointment.
accepted.sec: Constitutional, statutory and executive appointments

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Cabinet Secretary:
1. The post is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet.
2. The normal term is two years and it may be extended up to four years.
3. The Cabinet Secretary ranks 11th in the order of precedence.
4. The Cabinet Secretary heads the National Crisis Management Committee.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Cabinet Secretary is appointed by the ACC, has a two-year term extendable to four years, ranks 11th and heads the NCMC.
accepted.tq: Verify each institutional detail before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Constitutional, statutory and executive appointments

accepted.s: Under the 2023 law relating to the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners, the Selection Committee consists of:
o: Prime Minister, Chief Justice of India and the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
Prime Minister, Union Home Minister and Chief Election Commissioner
President, Prime Minister and Chief Justice of India
Prime Minister, Leader of the Opposition and a Union Cabinet Minister
accepted.x: The 2023 Act provides for a Selection Committee comprising the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and a Union Cabinet Minister. The Chief Justice of India was removed from the panel.
accepted.tq: Use the statutory composition and reject the earlier judicial-member arrangement.
accepted.sec: Constitutional, statutory and executive appointments

accepted.s: The tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners is:
o: Five years or until the age of 62, whichever is earlier
Six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier
Five years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier
Six years without an age limit
accepted.x: The tenure is six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier.
accepted.tq: Check both components of a tenure rule: duration and age limit.
accepted.sec: Constitutional, statutory and executive appointments

accepted.s: The Supreme Court described the Chief Justice of India’s place on the CEC selection panel as temporary in May 2026, referring to the arrangement arising from:
accepted.x: The temporary inclusion of the Chief Justice of India arose from the Anoop Baranwal decision of March 2023, as clarified by the Supreme Court in May 2026.
accepted.tq: Link the later clarification with the specific earlier judicial decision.
accepted.sec: Constitutional, statutory and executive appointments

accepted.s: Who is the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha in 2026?
accepted.x: Harivansh Narayan Singh is the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the presiding office from the Leader of Opposition and other constitutional posts.
accepted.sec: Constitutional, statutory and executive appointments

accepted.s: Which of the following was unprecedented in relation to the Deputy Chairmanship of the Rajya Sabha?
o: A nominated member became the first Deputy Chairman without a parliamentary vote.
The Deputy Chairman was appointed by the Chief Justice of India.
A nominated member was elected to the office for a third consecutive term.
The office was held simultaneously by two members.
accepted.x: For the first time, a nominated member was elected Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha for a third consecutive term.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise constitutional-parliamentary novelty rather than a general appointment detail.
accepted.sec: Constitutional, statutory and executive appointments

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs of State and Chief Minister is correctly matched?
accepted.x: C. Joseph Vijay became Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu. Suvendu Adhikari is associated with West Bengal and D.K. Shivakumar with Karnataka.
accepted.tq: Begin with the State–Chief Minister pair and eliminate cross-State substitutions.
accepted.sec: Constitutional, statutory and executive appointments

accepted.s: Who was appointed Director of the Intelligence Bureau in June 2026?
accepted.x: Mahesh Dixit, a 1993-batch Andhra Pradesh-cadre IPS officer, was appointed IB Director in June 2026.
accepted.tq: Match the appointment with the service background and month of appointment.
accepted.sec: Constitutional, statutory and executive appointments

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: IB Director — Gen. N.S. Raja Subramani
accepted.x: Gen. N.S. Raja Subramani is the Chief of Defence Staff, whereas Mahesh Dixit is the IB Director. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Use the service and office distinction to catch a swapped appointment.
accepted.sec: Constitutional, statutory and executive appointments

accepted.s: Gen. Dhiraj Seth became the 31st Chief of the Army Staff on:
accepted.x: Gen. Dhiraj Seth became the 31st Chief of the Army Staff on 1 July 2026.
accepted.tq: Combine the serial number with the exact date of assumption of office.
accepted.sec: Constitutional, statutory and executive appointments

accepted.s: Who was the Vice Chief of the Army Staff when Gen. Dhiraj Seth became Chief of the Army Staff?
accepted.x: Lt Gen Sandeep Jain was the Vice Chief of the Army Staff.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Vice Chief of the Army from the Vice Chief of the Navy.
accepted.sec: Constitutional, statutory and executive appointments

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Indian Navy’s senior appointments?
1. Adm. Krishna Swaminathan is the 27th Chief of the Naval Staff.
2. Vice Adm. Ajay Kochhar is the 48th Vice Chief of the Naval Staff.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
accepted.x: Both statements are correct: Krishna Swaminathan is the 27th CNS and Ajay Kochhar is the 48th VCNS.
accepted.tq: Test paired serial numbers within the same service hierarchy.
accepted.sec: Constitutional, statutory and executive appointments

accepted.s: Mallikarjun Kharge was reappointed in June 2026 as the:
o: Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha
Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
accepted.x: Mallikarjun Kharge was reappointed Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha in June 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the chamber and office in parliamentary appointments.
accepted.sec: Constitutional, statutory and executive appointments
